note: Every external dataset Sauron pulls from, with its link, licence and what it gives us. Add a row here before adding a field to the pipeline.

sources.name: Nominatim reverse geocoding
sources.cost: free, no key, capped at 1 request/second by the usage policy
sources.caveats: Only fills a field that is still null; never overwrites a value OSM tags or RERA already supplied. Every response is cached by society id in data/.cache-nominatim.json so a rerun only fetches what is missing. 'Suburb' in this data is usually the GBA ward name, which doubles as the well known locality name here, so it is used as a fallback once neighbourhood and quarter are ruled out. Candidates that just echo the society's own OSM name back are discarded.

sources.name: OpenStreetMap, via the Overpass API
sources.caveats: Uneven coverage. Strong on large older townships, thin on recent launches. Police and fire station coverage is incomplete.

sources.name: Greater Bengaluru Authority ward boundaries and reservations, 2026
sources.origin: Government of Karnataka final ward notification, 7 March 2026
gives: ward name in English and Kannada
sources.caveats: Reservation status changes with each election cycle. Boundaries are the March 2026 final set.

sources.name: Karnataka RERA project register
sources.origin: https://rera.karnataka.gov.in, scraped into 8,791 projects and 174 columns
sources.licence: ODbL 1.0, some content copyright Karnataka RERA
sources.caveats: Post 2017 registrations only. Unit counts populated on 34 percent of rows, coordinates on 46 percent; a filing with no unit count is still added rather than dropped. The official portal is slow and often unreachable, which is why the mirror is used. A filing outside every GBA ward polygon but within 15 km of the notified boundary still gets the nearest ward, flagged ward.approx: true, since the March 2026 notification does not yet reach every real Bengaluru launch (Sarjapur, Attibele, Anekal outskirts).

sources.name: CARTO basemaps
sources.licence: Free with attribution to OpenStreetMap contributors and CARTO

sources.name: Esri World Imagery
sources.licence: Free to display with attribution. Bulk download and storage are not permitted.
gives: site and context aerials saved per society

sources.name: Wikimedia Commons geosearch
sources.licence: CC, per file. Author and licence recorded in the image index.
sources.caveats: Thin coverage of Bengaluru societies. A file is kept only when its name or description mentions the society or its builder.

sources.name: BBMP street lights by ward
sources.licence: OpenCity, no licence stated. Treat as public sector information.
gives: street light count for each of the 198 old BBMP wards
sources.caveats: Counted against the old 198 ward map, so it is apportioned onto the 369 GBA wards by area. 64 new wards fall outside the counted area and are left null. Undated in the source.

sources.name: BBMP ward boundaries, 2022 and 2023
gives: old ward polygons, needed to move ward level data onto the new map

sources.name: Bengaluru crime data, city totals
sources.origin: Bengaluru City Police, from FIRs filed
gives: reported and detected counts by crime type for 2021, 2022 and 2023
separate tables for crimes against women, crimes against children, cyber crime, accidental and suicide deaths
sources.caveats: City wide totals only. No ward, station or point geography, so it cannot drive a heat map on its own.

sources.name: Karnataka State Police crime data, 2022 to 2025
gives: crimes against women, children and SC/ST
sources.caveats: District and commissionerate granularity at best. Station level tables exist only inside the Crime Review PDFs.

sources.name: Bing News RSS
gives: headline, snippet, publisher, publication date and article link for an exact-name query
sources.caveats: Primary daily source. Bing redirect links are unwrapped to publisher URLs. Results are retained only when the entity name is visible in the headline or RSS snippet. The RSS response limits use to private, non-commercial aggregation, which matches this internal tool.

sources.name: GDELT 2.0 Document API
sources.licence: Unlimited and unrestricted academic, commercial or governmental use with citation
gives: news articles by keyword and date, back to 2017, with publisher, date and URL
sources.caveats: One request every 5 seconds, and in practice sometimes unreachable or rate limited from a shared network. It is the daily fallback when Bing RSS is unavailable. Results are retained only when the entity name is visible in the headline or snippet.

sources.name: Google News RSS
sources.licence: Headlines and links only, no full text
gives: headline, publisher, date and link for a query
sources.caveats: The more reliable of the two in practice, since GDELT is often unreachable. Titles are Google's own headline plus publisher, dates are RSS pubDate.

sources.name: Bengaluru City Police station contacts
gives: police station names, jurisdictions and phone numbers
used_by: planned: cross check of the OSM station list

sources.name: Bengaluru Traffic Police, station wise road crashes
gives: crashes, fatal crashes, killed and injured per traffic police station, 2018 to 2025
sources.caveats: Road safety, not crime. Station names are abbreviated and spelled inconsistently between years, so the join runs through an alias list. Stations created after 2022 have no polygon.

sources.name: Bengaluru Traffic Police jurisdictions
sources.caveats: 2022 vintage, so it predates the stations added since.

sources.name: Bengaluru CCTV camera locations
gives: camera points owned by traffic police, city police and BBMP, crowdsourced from OSM
sources.caveats: Non commercial licence, so check before it goes into anything sold. Crowdsourced, so coverage is partial.

sources.name: Bengaluru and Karnataka fire stations
sources.caveats: Worth swapping in for the 29 stations OSM knows about.

considered_not_used.name: Property portals: Housing, 99acres, MagicBricks, NoBroker, CommonFloor
considered_not_used.why_not: Terms forbid scraping and the sites run bot protection. Needs a licence or partnership.

considered_not_used.name: Licensed project data: PropEquity, Liases Foras, CRE Matrix, PropTiger
considered_not_used.why_not: Would close the coverage gap on recent launches and give unit mix and pricing. Roughly ₹1 lakh to ₹5 lakh a year for Bengaluru.

considered_not_used.name: News: Deccan Herald, TOI Bengaluru, The Hindu, Bangalore Mirror direct
considered_not_used.why_not: GDELT and Google News RSS already index these outlets, so a per publisher scrape would mostly duplicate scrape/13-news.js for more engineering effort. Revisit only if a publisher's stories are not turning up through either.

considered_not_used.name: Bengaluru City Police
considered_not_used.why_not: Station and ward level statistics only, not society level. Useful to cross check the OSM station list.

considered_not_used.name: Google Places photos
considered_not_used.why_not: Needs a billed key, and the terms treat photo bytes as content you may not store. Script parked at scrape/optional/google-images.js.

considered_not_used.name: Station level crime counts
considered_not_used.why_not: Not published anywhere reachable. The Bengaluru 2023 press note and the 54 page Karnataka Crime Review both stop at city and district level: the finest geography in the Review is commissionerate and range. ksp.karnataka.gov.in and bcp.karnataka.gov.in do not respond from this network. The realistic route is an RTI to the Commissioner for station wise FIR counts by head and year.

review.how_to_refresh: Run the numbered scripts in scrape/ in order. Each one caches its download in data/.cache-*; delete the cache file to force a fresh pull.
watch_for: GBA ward boundaries change with each delimitation. Re-pull the KML and rerun 02 and 04.
Karnataka RERA mirror updates when its maintainer reruns the scrape. Check the repo's last commit before trusting the unit counts as current.
Crime data is published annually. A 2026 Bengaluru release would replace the 2023 file.
Builder websites move project pages. 08 records what it could not find in data/images-missing.json.
